body:
Global crypto market cap sits at $2.7T today, down 2.51% over 24 hours despite most individual tokens printing green — a divergence that tells you there's been rotation and profit-taking running beneath a surface that looks calmer than it is. Total 24-hour volume came in at $67.1B, a respectable figure that suggests participation without mania. The Fear & Greed index held flat at 73 on both today and yesterday, squarely in Greed territory, meaning the crowd hasn't flinched yet — but flat sentiment readings after a negative market-cap day are worth noting, because complacency and conviction look identical until they don't.

BTC is trading at $79,915, up just 0.37% over 24 hours and 2.60% on the week, but the headline that matters today came from Cointelegraph: a surprise nonfarm payrolls print sent Bitcoin back below $80,000. That level is now the line in the sand. A clean reclaim and hold above $80,000 on meaningful volume restores the bull case for a run at the next resistance cluster; a continued rejection here and BTC dominance at 59.2% becomes a liability rather than a pillar of strength. Bitcoin ETF inflows hitting $3.8B in the strongest 3-week stretch of 2026, per Cointelegraph, remains the structural bid underneath, but macro-driven spot selling can absolutely overwhelm ETF flows on a session-by-session basis.

ETH at $2,501.59 is quietly outperforming bitcoin on the day, up 1.95% with $8.78B in volume, and its 7-day return of 2.00% matches SOL's weekly print exactly. The real altcoin story today is in UNI, DOT, and LINK. UNI is the standout at $7.01, up 12.26% on the day and an extraordinary 45.10% over 7 days on volume of $1.09B — that kind of move in a DeFi governance token demands a closer look at whether protocol-level news is driving it or whether it's simply the last leg of a momentum trade getting crowded. DOT broke above the psychologically important $1.00 level intraday before settling at $0.973074, up 7.28% on the day and 15.10% on the week, with LINK adding 4.55% to trade at $12.27. BNB's 7-day gain of 9.40% to $757.62 is also notable, though today's 24-hour move of 0.73% suggests the weekly energy is fading. SOL at $106.54, up 4.13% on the day, continues to act well relative to the broader tape.

The macro driver today is unambiguous: the surprise nonfarm payrolls print rattled risk assets and pushed BTC back below $80,000 intraday. A stronger-than-expected labor print reduces the Fed's urgency to cut rates, which compresses the multiple on risk assets across the board and strengthens the dollar — a direct headwind for crypto priced in USD. The Bank of Korea published a study flagging that dollar-backed stablecoins can push local currencies lower, which adds a layer of regulatory sensitivity in Asia at a time when Southeast Asia's crypto funding is rebounding to $680M according to CoinDesk. Poland upholding a crypto bill veto amid the Zondacrypto scandal, per Cointelegraph, is a reminder that European regulatory momentum is not uniformly constructive. The Tether-backed Orionx shutting down after an audit flagged a $7M custody gap is a minor but real confidence signal to monitor in the stablecoin infrastructure space.

The immediate catalyst to track is whether BTC can reclaim and sustain $80,000 — that single level resolves the near-term directional debate. Watch how ETF flow data evolves through the week; if the 3-week inflow streak continues despite today's macro headwind, institutional demand is absorbing the payrolls shock and the dip is buyable. On the risk side, any follow-through dollar strength or additional hot macro prints before the next Fed meeting would pressure the $79,000 to $80,000 range significantly. UNI's 45.10% 7-day move needs a fundamental explanation or it becomes a distribution event; traders long DeFi tokens should be watching volume profiles carefully. The XRP Ledger data showing fewer active accounts despite larger individual trade sizes, per CoinDesk, is a maturation signal but also a liquidity concentration risk — worth watching if XRP, currently at $1.42, encounters selling pressure.
